tests/test_bridges/test_hex_editor_top_a.recommendation: Replace with test_get_display_mode_blocks_while_set_document_holds_lock pattern: launch set_document() with slow operations in a thread while attempting get_display_mode() from another thread, asserting the getter blocks until the lock is released. tests/test_bridges/test_hex_editor_top_a.why_not_gate: The test verifies the observable end-state (bridge.document is None) but cannot detect lock removal. The lock's purpose is to serialize concurrent access to document/cursor/selection during mutation, but this test only observes the mutation's completion, not its serialization. A concurrent reader accessing bridge.document while close_file() clears it (without the lock) would see torn state, but this test never attempts concurrent access.

tests/test_bridges/test_hex_editor_top_a.recommendation: Use a PE fixture with actual imports (kernel32.dll, user32.dll functions). If the production code were changed to always use the memory path (dropping the disk-path optimization), the MZ pattern would still match and the test would pass. The test does not verify which scan path was taken.

tests/test_bridges/test_hex_state_audit1.recommendation: Replace with a blocking-semantics test like test_get_display_mode_blocks_while_set_document_holds_lock (line 513+): start a thread running set_document() with a known slow operation (e.g., via mock), then from another thread call get_display_mode() and measure that it blocks for the duration of the slow operation. Assert that get_display_mode() cannot proceed until set_document() releases the lock. This proves symmetric lock acquisition/release between getter and setter.
tests/test_bridges/test_hex_state_audit1.why_not_gate: On CPython, the Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) makes the read and write of a single string reference atomic at the machine level. The assertion all(value in allowed for value in samples) checks that every observed value is one of the three short allowed strings. Even if the lock were removed entirely from set_display_mode_state() and get_display_mode(), any torn read of the _display_mode string reference would still yield one of the three published values (no third state exists between them), so the assertion can never fail. The locking contract F-0038 is designed to prevent observing intermediate torn state, but CPython's GIL makes that intermediate state unobservable at the test level. This test does not actually exercise the lock's protecting behavior.
